prompt: The point $(1, 1)$ sits on $y = x^2$. The graph is stretched to $y = 4x^2$. On the new graph, what is the $y$-value when $x = 1$?
hint: A number multiplying the whole function stretches the graph taller.

hints.text: A number multiplying the whole function stretches the graph taller.
Find $x^2$ first when $x = 1$, then multiply that answer by $4$.

explanation: In $a \cdot f(x)$, every $y$-value is multiplied by $a$.
Here $a = 4$, so heights become $4$ times bigger.

alternativeExplanations.title: A table of heights
steps: Every height is exactly 4 times taller — the sticker got stretched, not slid.
